title: Signature Path-Condition Archive
description: Signature edition: every explored path's condition is archived with its test input and the code version — a permanent map of which inputs drive which paths. When code changes, the archive shows exactly which paths' conditions changed, focusing re-testing where behavior moved. This is a Signature original method.
method: Archive (path condition, input, code version) per path; diff conditions across versions; re-test only changed paths.
usage: Archive per release; diff on change; let the archive focus regression testing.

demo.code:
print('v2.3: 47 paths archived')
print('v2.4: 3 path conditions changed -> re-test those 3, others inherit PASS')

title: Signature Concolic execution (DART/CUTE)
description: Signature edition: Concolic = concrete + symbolic: run the program concretely while tracking symbolic constraints alongside. When the concrete run takes a branch, negate that branch's constraint and solve for an input that takes the other way — systematically driving execution toward uncovered paths. DART pioneered it; SAGE used it to fuzz Windows at scale.
method: Concrete run + symbolic shadow; collect path constraint; negate one branch; solve for new input; repeat toward coverage.
usage: Seed with valid inputs (concolic needs a starting run); let the negations explore from there.

demo.code:
print('concrete: x=5 takes else-branch; constraint {x<=10}')
print('negate -> solve {x>10} -> x=11 takes if-branch: new path covered')

title: Signature Under-constrained symbolic execution
description: Signature edition: Full-program symbolic execution drowns in environment complexity; under-constrained execution analyzes one function in isolation with symbolic inputs and lazy initialization of pointers. It finds real bugs in individual functions fast — trading whole-program soundness for targeted bug hunting.
method: Start at the target function; inputs fully symbolic; lazily initialize pointed-to memory; report bugs with the under-constrained caveat.
usage: Use for triaging suspicious functions; confirm findings with more precise analysis.

demo.code:
print('analyze parse_header() alone: inputs symbolic')
print('found: null deref on malformed header -> confirmed in full context')

title: Signature Symbolic execution for test generation
description: Signature edition: Every explored path yields concrete inputs that drive that path — an automatic high-coverage test suite. KLEE on Coreutils found real bugs and generated tests no human wrote. For parsers, protocols, and utilities, symbolic test generation beats hand-written tests on coverage per effort.
method: Explore paths; solve each path's constraints; emit (input, expected-path) as tests; minimize the suite.
usage: Generate, minimize, and check in the suite; re-generate when the code changes significantly.

demo.code:
print('parser: 47 paths explored -> 47 tests generated')
print('coverage: 96% branches (hand-written suite: 71%)')

title: Signature Veritesting (static+dynamic merge)
description: Signature edition: Veritesting statically merges straight-line code regions into single path constraints, so the dynamic engine forks only at genuinely hard branches. Developed for the Mayhem system (CMU), it tames path explosion in binary analysis by letting static analysis do the easy merging.
method: Statically recover CFG; merge bounded regions into formulas; dynamic execution handles the rest; fewer forks, same coverage.
usage: Use for binary analysis at scale; the static recovery quality bounds the benefit.

demo.code:
print('function: 200 branches, mostly straight-line')
print('veritesting merges 180 statically -> dynamic forks only 20')

title: Signature Guided symbolic execution toward targets
description: Signature edition: Instead of exploring everywhere, directed symbolic execution aims at a target — a patched line, a dangerous sink, a crash site. Distance metrics on the CFG guide the search; the solver only works on paths that can reach the target. Bug hunting with a destination.
method: Compute CFG distance to target; prioritize states by distance; prune states that can't reach the target; solve on arrival.
usage: Define targets precisely (line numbers, sink calls); combine with patch-diff to check only changed code's reachability.

demo.code:
print('target: memcpy at line 88 (patched)')
print('guided search: 12 states pruned, target reached in 40s')
print('input reaching patch: generated for regression test')

title: Signature SMT solver integration
description: Signature edition: The solver is the engine's oracle: every branch feasibility check, every test-input generation is an SMT query. Solver choice and query shaping (incremental solving, constraint caching, independent-constraint splitting) determine whether the engine runs for minutes or days.
method: Incremental solver sessions; cache query results; split independent constraints; choose solver per theory (bitvectors vs arrays).
usage: Profile solver time first when the engine is slow; enable caching and incremental modes.

demo.code:
print('query cache hit rate 78% -> solver time 41min -> 9min')
print('independent constraint splitting: 3 sub-queries, parallel')

title: Signature Path explosion mitigations
description: Signature edition: Symbolic execution's enemy is path explosion: 2^n paths for n branches. Mitigations — state merging (join paths with disjunctive constraints), bounded exploration, search heuristics (coverage-guided), and veritesting (merge static paths) — make real programs analyzable instead of theoretically analyzable.
method: Merge states at join points; bound loops/depth; prioritize by coverage heuristic; use veritesting for straight-line regions.
usage: Combine mitigations; no single one suffices; measure coverage per technique to see what pays.

demo.code:
print('10 branches: 1024 paths -> merged at joins: 24 states')
print('path explosion contained via state merging')

title: Signature Environment modeling
description: Signature edition: Real programs call the environment — files, network, syscalls. Symbolic executors model these (symbolic files in KLEE, models of libc) so analysis doesn't stop at the first read() call. Good environment models are what separate toy demos from tools that handle real code.
method: Model syscalls/files symbolically; keep models faithful but simple; concretize where modeling is infeasible.
usage: Invest in models for the syscalls your target uses; document model limitations as analysis caveats.

demo.code:
print('read(fd, buf, n): symbolic file returns symbolic bytes')
print('analysis continues past I/O instead of stopping')
